title: add-init-ownership-lock-and-graceful-rollback-gate
text:
add-init-ownership-lock-and-graceful-rollback-gate

body:
Motivation: Private installs with many tenants observed transient failures and stuck upgrades when multiple init hooks / migration jobs ran concurrently or were preempted during rollbacks. This PR introduces a lightweight ownership lock and a graceful rollback gate to ensure at-most-one active init orchestrator per tenant/namespace and to avoid tearing down resources mid-migration. Summary of changes: 1) templates/init-ownership-lock.yaml: new ConfigMap+annotations pattern to act as a namespaced lease that the init orchestrator can tryAcquire/release; it's implemented with a small TTL annotation and a controller-friendly ownerLabel so the init job can verify leadership before applying migration work. 2) templates/init-orchestrator-deployment.yaml: a small sidecar-compatible init orchestrator that respects ownership lock, exposes a simple /healthz and emits events when acquiring/releasing the lock. It is optional and enabled via values.init.orchestrator.enabled=false by default. 3) templates/rollback-guard-crd.yaml + helpers: a templated guard in Helm that writes a block annotation onto the release when an init orchestrator is active; Helm hooks and the upgrade pipeline consult this annotation to delay or fail immediate rollbacks unless override.confirm=true is set in values. 4) values.schema.json: introduce init.control and rollback.guard sections with validation (maxConcurrency, lockTTL, safeRollbackWindow, overrideKey). 5) charts/tests: a pair of Helm tests that simulate concurrent init jobs to validate lock behavior and a rollback test that verifies the guard prevents unsafe rollbacks in CI. 6) docs/installer/upgrade-guides/init-lock.md: operational notes and recovery steps, including how to force-release an orphaned lock. Checklist: - [x] Design doc in Linear (ENG-1428) - [x] Values.schema addition and unit tests - [x] Helm template implementation and linting - [x] Integration Helm tests in CI - [x] Reviewed and approved by SRE and Installer teams (see comments) - [x] Backed out of main for a small hotfix during rollout (see discussion) Implementation notes and rationale: - We chose a ConfigMap lease instead of introducing a separate Kubernetes Lease CRD to keep compatibility with clusters that have restricted RBAC for coordination objects. The lock uses timestamp annotation and an ownerLabel to allow manual reconciliation. - The rollback gate writes a release-level annotation (redwood.io/init-active="true|<owner>") that the installer pipeline checks; this avoids embedding cluster-level sidecars into the lifecycle manager. - The orchestrator respects values.init.orchestrator.maxConcurrency per-node and uses a simple exponential backoff for acquisiton retries; defaults are conservative to avoid thundering-herd in large tenant clusters. - We added a values.rollback.guard.safeRollbackWindow default of 5m to allow in-flight init jobs to finish before a rollback proceeds; operators can override but must set overrideKey to allow emergency rollbacks. Operational considerations and migration path: - Default behavior is off for clusters that don't opt in; enabling is a single toggle in values.yaml. - For existing installations, operators can install this chart upgrade in dry-run first; preservation of current release behavior is the default. - If a lock becomes orphaned (controller crashed), operators can force-release using kubectl patch on the ConfigMap or via a new CLI helper documented in docs. Testing: - Unit tests cover values.schema shape and template rendering for edge cases. - Integration test runs in the installer CI (helm test) simulate 3 concurrent init jobs; lock is acquired by one and others backoff. - Rollback guard test simulates an in-progress init and ensures helm rollback is blocked unless override.confirm=true. Rollout plan: staged rollout to beta tenants first, then to all tenants after 48h monitoring. See linked Linear ENG-1499 for the monitor/rollback playbook.

release_notes:
Add an init ownership lock and rollback gate to reduce tenant init collisions and prevent unsafe rollbacks; extend values.schema with init.control and rollback.guard settings.

discussion_summary:
Consensus to prefer ConfigMap-based lock for compatibility; rollback gate accepted as opt-in with overrideKey for emergencies. Staged rollout required; SRE to monitor init failure ratio for 48h after rollout. Backout route documented.

review_comments:
Luca Moretti (2024-11-06): Left a few nits around lock TTL calculation and suggested using RFC3339 timestamps for annotation values. Also asked for clarifying the safeRollbackWindow semantics; resolved in followup commit.
Priya Nair (2024-11-07): Requested that the default for init.orchestrator.enabled be false to avoid surprising behavior during upgrades — set to false and documented. Approved after tests.
Ethan Zhang (2024-11-09): Noted an edge case where leader churn could happen when controllers are scheduled on preemptible nodes; suggested adding jitter to retries. Added jitter and the addition was tested in the helm test.
Maya Patel (2024-11-11): Responded to review comments and pushed small fixes for schema validation errors and README clarifications.
